caption: What if salt touched a slug? A slug is a snail whose tiny shell is hidden under its skin, and its eyes sit on the tips of its long tentacles (lose one and it can regrow it). Its skin loses water easily, so it stays coated in slime. Salt dissolves in that slime and makes it saltier than the slug's insides. Water always flows toward the saltier side, which is osmosis, so water gets pulled out of the slug. It pumps out foamy slime to wash the salt off, but enough salt dries it out within minutes. Please never do this to a slug. The same trick protects your achaar: salt pulls water out of microbes so they can't grow. It's also why you can't drink seawater (about 3.5% salt): your kidneys can't make urine saltier than your blood. Plot twist: sea slugs live in salt water all day, because their insides are about as salty as the sea. Which salty fact surprised YOU? 👇
